title: Dispatch TUR 3: Engineer Reveals Missing Page in Westmere Plans
summary: The abandoned line was designed with a terminus omitted from every public map.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Mr. Wren arrived at the Institute carrying the Westmere timetable plate and a folded plan inherited from his grandfather, who surveyed the railway. The plan shows a final platform beneath the Alderwick goods depot. Its entrance would have stood where a locked coal cellar stands today.

On the back is a note in the surveyor’s hand: “The terminus is to be left unannounced until the marsh foundations are proved.” The foundations were never proved. Mr. Wren says his family kept the plan because it was the only surviving drawing of the company’s intended end point.

Dr. Saye and Mr. Pike entered the coal cellar yesterday. They found bare brick, a blocked drain, and a square of floor worn smooth in the shape of a station clock. A train bell sounded twice while they were below ground. Both heard it; a third witness at the street entrance heard nothing.

The newest letters have ceased to concern tea and birthdays. One from a porter at North Wicket reports that the marsh is rising around the line. Another tells a family in Alderwick that the last service will carry evacuees from Kingsfen on 17 October 1894. Its writer urges the recipients not to wait for the second train.

An unsigned note found inside the same sack contains a single instruction: “Tell the terminus there is a train coming.” Mr. Pike believes it was written by someone on the railway. Dr. Saye asks a harder question: whether the cellar can receive a train if Alderwick refuses to acknowledge it as a station.
